{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level factor, using Type III sums of squares",
    "For Success (binary), use logistic regression or chi-square test of independence rather than ANOVA, as the mean of 0.73 with SD 0.44 indicates binary 0/1 coding",
    "Given substantial sample size imbalance across paradigms (Combined n=48846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3323), use Welch's ANOVA or verify homogeneity of variance assumption; if violated, use Welch's ANOVA with Games-Howell post-hoc",
    "Include Mouse as a random effect or blocking factor in mixed-effects models to account for 8 mice with repeated measures, as mouse-specific clustering (n=76655 total, 8 mice) may inflate Type I error if ignored"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For continuous outcomes with significant ANOVA results, perform pairwise comparisons between all 10 pairs of stimulation paradigms using estimated marginal means",
    "Report effect sizes (Cohen's d or partial eta-squared) alongside p-values to contextualize magnitude of differences given large sample sizes",
    "Prioritize comparisons of Combined vs single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and all active conditions vs Sham to address specific hypotheses about multimodal integration and stimulation efficacy",
    "For Success (binary), use pairwise chi-square tests with standardized residuals or logistic regression contrasts with appropriate link function"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Control family-wise error rate across the 10 pairwise comparisons per outcome using the Benjamini-Hochberg FDR procedure at alpha=0.05, rather than Bonferroni, to balance Type I and Type II error given the large sample size and exploratory nature; apply FDR separately within each of the 5 response variables to maintain interpretability",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Given that Stim Paradigm is categorical and the goal is prediction of paradigm from performance variables, recommend a multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as the categorical response and the five performance metrics as predictors. This is the appropriate categorical-response model: it estimates log-odds of each paradigm relative to a reference category (suggest Sham as baseline) while handling the nominal nature of the response. Alternative: random forest or gradient boosting for non-linear relationships and interactions, with cross-validation to assess generalizability. Do NOT use ordinary linear regression as it would impose false ordinality on the 5 paradigms. If interest is in which performance variables best discriminate paradigms, follow with multinomial discriminant analysis or multinomial probit for comparison.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Verify normality of residuals for each continuous outcome using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on subsamples given n>70000; consider log-transformation for Time-to-Target given max=201.39 vs mean=2.81 indicating right skew",
    "Assess homogeneity of variance using Levene's test; given unequal group sizes (ratio ~15:1), Welch's ANOVA is preferred a priori",
    "Check for multicollinearity among predictors in multinomial model (e.g., Path Efficiency and Average Speed may correlate) using VIF; consider dimensionality reduction if r>0.7",
    "Evaluate independence assumption: given repeated measures from 8 mice, use mixed-effects models or cluster-robust standard errors to account for within-mouse correlation",
    "For multinomial logistic regression, verify independence of irrelevant alternatives (IIA) assumption using Hausman-McFadden test or consider nested logit if violated"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, higher Average Speed, lower AD) compared to single-modality conditions, consistent with multisensory integration benefits",
    "ICMS Only may outperform visual-only conditions given direct cortical engagement, though this depends on task demands",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance across metrics, serving as baseline for effect size calibration",
    "Dim Visual Only vs Bright Visual Only may differ if luminance affects visibility; Dim may impair performance relative to Bright",
    "Large sample sizes will yield statistically significant differences even for small effects; emphasize effect sizes and confidence intervals over p-values",
    "Multinomial model likely shows highest classification accuracy for Combined vs Sham, with intermediate confusion among single-modality conditions"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in paradigm allocation (Combined 63.7% of data vs Bright Visual Only 4.3%) reduces precision for rare conditions and may bias variance estimates; consider stratified sampling or weighting in predictive models",
    "No trial-level temporal information available to account for learning effects or fatigue across the session",
    "Mouse identity confounded with potential cohort or surgical differences; 8 mice provide limited generalizability",
    "AD (angular dispersion) interpretation uncertain without explicit definition—assumed to measure path tortuosity or directional variability with lower values indicating straighter paths",
    "Temperature=0.0 and model=kimi in run metadata suggest LLM-generated or deterministic predictions rather than biological data; verify data provenance if this affects inference validity",
    "Success as binary outcome loses information about near-misses vs complete failures; consider ordinal or time-to-event models if granular data exist"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as response, the five performance metrics as fixed effects, and Mouse as random intercept, using Bayesian estimation (e.g., brms in R) to obtain regularized estimates given group imbalance; accompany with permutation-based importance scores and partial dependence plots to identify which performance variables most strongly discriminate paradigms, particularly for distinguishing Combined from ICMS Only where collinearity may challenge interpretation."
}
